title.zh: 辞婚：一次被安排的试探与吴起离开魏国
title.en: Refusing the Bride: A Staged Test and Wu Qi's Departure from Wei

dek.zh: 在魏国任西河守、功劳明确的吴起，因为一桩被安排的婚事失去了君主的信任，随即去了楚国。让他离开的不是战场胜负，而是一件被设计的小事。
dek.en: He had held Wei's western frontier at Xihe, and his record was not in dispute. Then an arranged marriage cost him his ruler's trust, and he left for Chu. What drove him out was not a battle but a piece of stagecraft.

heading.zh: 一件家常事，做成了一场判决
heading.en: A Domestic Detail Made Into a Verdict

paras.zh: 吴起在魏国做西河守，抵御秦、韩；但真正让他决定离开魏国的，不是一场败仗，而是一桩婚事——他拒绝娶魏国公主，武侯随即不再信他，他很快去了楚国。
paras.en: Wu Qi governed the district of Xihe for Wei, holding the frontier against Qin and Han. Yet what finally pushed him out of Wei was not a lost battle but a marriage. He refused to take a Wei princess as his wife; Marquis Wu stopped trusting him; and before long Wu Qi had gone to the state of Chu.

paras.zh: 值得注意的是，这次转折里几乎没有任何胜负可记。设计者用一件家常小事做钩子，把“留不留心”这个说不清的问题，换成一个看得见的动作。一种解释是：正因为试探太小，被试探者很难把“拒绝”说成一件大事去解释。（作者解释）
paras.en: In the author's reading, almost nothing in this turn of events can be scored as a victory or a defeat. The man who set the trap used an ordinary household matter as bait, converting an unanswerable question — did he mean to stay? — into an act everyone could see. One explanation: precisely because the test is so small, the man being tested cannot easily turn his refusal into a large matter to be explained.

heading.zh: 上一次被疑，也是一桩婚事
heading.en: The Last Time He Was Suspected, It Was Also a Marriage

paras.zh: 吴起是卫国人，好用兵，曾从曾子学习，在鲁国做事。齐国攻打鲁国，鲁国想用他为将，麻烦出在他的妻子是齐国人，鲁国因此疑心他。为了表明自己与齐国无关，他杀掉妻子，鲁国这才用他为将；他领兵攻齐，大破齐军。
paras.en: Wu Qi was a man of the state of Wey (衛 — distinct from Wei 魏, the state he would later serve), devoted to the art of war. He had studied under the philosopher Zengzi and served the ruler of Lu. When Qi attacked Lu, Lu wanted him as commander; the trouble was that his wife was a woman of Qi, and Lu suspected him. To show that he had no bond with Qi, he killed his wife. Lu then made him commander, he marched against Qi, and he smashed its army.

paras.zh: 胜仗之后，鲁国有人在鲁君面前这样描述他：为人猜忍；年轻时家累千金，外出求官不成，散尽家财，被乡党笑话，他杀掉三十多个讥讽自己的人，从卫国郭门向东出走；与母亲诀别时啮臂立誓，不做卿相不回卫国；后来母亲去世，他始终没有回去，曾子因此与他断绝关系。进言者还算了另一笔账：鲁国是小国，有了战胜之名，诸侯就要图谋鲁国；鲁卫是兄弟之国，用吴起等于抛弃卫国。这里所据的原文止于这段进言，没有记载鲁君听后如何处置。
paras.en: After the victory, a courtier described him to the ruler of Lu like this: a suspicious, ruthless man. In his youth his family was worth a fortune; he went off seeking office, failed, and ran through the family fortune, until his neighbors laughed at him. He then killed more than thirty of those who had mocked him and went out eastward through the outer gate of Wey's city wall. Parting from his mother, he bit his arm and swore he would not return to Wey until he became a high minister or chancellor. She died, and he never went back, whereupon Zengzi broke with him. The speech then turned to the arithmetic: Lu is a small state, and once it carries the name of a victory, the other lords will begin to plot against Lu. Lu and Wey are brother states; to employ Wu Qi is to abandon Wey. The text relied on here ends with this speech and records nothing of how the ruler of Lu responded.

paras.zh: 把这段进言拆开看，它没有否定吴起会打仗——否定的是他的“人”和用他的“账”：私德有亏，母死不归；小国担不起战胜之名。作者推断，这套说法的着力点，是把“他能不能打”换成了“我们要不起他”。原文没有写吴起对这次被疑的反应，本文也不替他补写。（作者解释）
paras.en: Notice what the speech never says: it does not deny that Wu Qi can fight. It attacks the man and the ledger of using him — a flaw in private character, no return home at his mother's death, a small state that cannot afford a reputation for victory. The author infers that the thrust of the speech is to swap one question for another: not can he win, but can we afford him. The source records no reaction from Wu Qi to this suspicion, and this article will not write one for him.

heading.en: From Sucking an Abscess to Refusing a Bride

paras.zh: 后来，魏文侯问李克吴起是什么样的人，李克答：「起貪而好色，然用兵司馬穰苴不能過也。」吴起带兵时，与最下等的士卒穿同样的衣服、吃同样的饭；睡觉不铺席子，行军不骑马乘车，亲自背负粮食，与士卒分担劳苦。
paras.en: Later, Marquis Wen of Wei asked Li Ke what sort of man Wu Qi was. Li Ke replied — rendered here in translation — that Wu Qi was greedy and fond of women, but that in commanding troops even Sima Rangju could not surpass him. As a general, Wu Qi wore the same clothes and ate the same food as the lowest of his soldiers. He slept without a mat, rode neither horse nor cart on the march, wrapped and carried his own share of grain, and shared the men's toil and hardship.

paras.zh: 有一个生痈疽的士卒，吴起为他吮吸患处。士卒的母亲听说后哭了。旁人不解：将军亲自为你儿子吮疽，哭什么？母亲说，往年吴公也为这孩子的父亲吮过疽，他父亲作战时脚跟不转、向前战死在敌阵；如今吴公又吮她的儿子，她不知道这孩子会死在哪里，所以哭。作者认为，这是本文里最刺眼的一笔：得士心的方式和它的代价，写在同一段哭声里。
paras.en: One soldier developed a carbuncle, and Wu Qi sucked the poison from it himself. The soldier's mother heard of this and wept. Someone asked her why she wept, when the general himself had tended her son's carbuncle. Her answer, given here in translation and paraphrase: it was not as they thought. Years ago Lord Wu had done the same for the boy's father, who then went into battle without turning on his heels and died at the enemy's hands. Now Lord Wu had done it again for her son, and she did not know where this child would meet his death. That was why she wept. In the author's reading, it is the most jarring stroke in the whole story: the way he won his men's hearts, and what that cost, are written in the same tears.

paras.zh: 魏文侯认为他善于用兵、廉平、能得士心，任命他为西河守，抵御秦、韩。后来武侯浮西河而下，中流回头对吴起感叹：「美哉乎山河之固，此魏國之寶也！」吴起的回答此处只节引其结尾：「由此觀之，在德不在險。若君不修德，舟中之人盡為敵國也。」武侯说「善」。
paras.en: Marquis Wen judged him skilled in war, honest and fair, and able to win the hearts of his men, and made him governor of Xihe to hold off Qin and Han. Once Marquis Wu was drifting down the West River; in midstream he turned to Wu Qi and exclaimed, in paraphrase, at how magnificent and secure the mountains and rivers were — a treasure of the state of Wei. Of Wu Qi's reply only its conclusion is given here, in translation: from this it can be seen that safety lies in virtue, not in natural defenses; if my lord does not cultivate virtue, everyone in this boat will become an enemy state. Marquis Wu approved, calling it well said.

paras.zh: 后来魏国置相，相田文，吴起不悦，提出与田文论功。他问：统率三军，使士卒乐死、敌国不敢谋，你比我如何？田文答「不如子」。又问：守住西河，秦兵不敢东向，韩赵宾从，你比我如何？田文仍答「不如子」。（原文共论三事，此处录其二。）吴起说，这三件事你都在我之下，位子却在我之上，为什么？
paras.en: In time Wei appointed a chancellor, and the office went to Tian Wen. Wu Qi was displeased and challenged him to compare their merits. In translation and paraphrase, the exchange runs as follows. Wu Qi asked how Tian Wen compared with him in commanding the three armies, making the soldiers glad to die, so that no enemy state dared to plot; Tian Wen said he was not his equal. Wu Qi asked how Tian Wen compared with him in holding Xihe, so that the armies of Qin dared not turn eastward and Han and Zhao came as obedient followers; again Tian Wen said he was not his equal. (The original weighs three matters; two are given here.) Wu Qi pressed the point: in all three of these Tian Wen fell below him, yet his rank stood above Wu Qi's — why?

paras.zh: 田文答：「主少國疑，大臣未附，百姓不信，方是之時，屬之於子乎？屬之於我乎？」吴起默然良久，说：「屬之子矣。」田文说，这正是我位居你之上的原因。原文接着写，吴起自知不如田文。
paras.en: Tian Wen answered — rendered here in translation — that the ruler was young and the state uncertain, the great ministers had not attached themselves to him, and the people did not trust him; at such a moment, should the state be entrusted to Wu Qi, or to Tian Wen? Wu Qi fell silent for a long time, then said it should be entrusted to Tian Wen. Tian Wen replied that this was precisely why he sat above Wu Qi. The source adds that Wu Qi knew himself the lesser of the two.

paras.zh: 田文死后，公叔为相，娶魏公主，想加害吴起。公叔的仆人说了一句很轻的话：「起易去也。」计策分两步。第一步是进言：吴起是贤人，而魏国小，又与强秦接壤，恐怕他没有长留之心；不妨以公主的婚事试探他——「起有留心則必受之。無留心則必辭矣。以此卜之。」第二步是安排：召吴起一同回家，令公主发怒、当面轻慢魏相。
paras.en: After Tian Wen died, Gongshu became chancellor; he had married a Wei princess, and he sought to harm Wu Qi. His servant said something very light — in translation, that Wu Qi was easy to remove. The scheme ran in two steps. First, a word to the marquis: Wu Qi is a man of talent, but Wei is a small state and borders mighty Qin; I fear he has no thought of staying. Test him with the offer of a princess — in the servant's words, rendered here in translation: if Wu Qi means to stay, he will certainly accept; if he has no such intention, he will certainly decline; use this to gauge him. Second, the arrangement: invite Wu Qi home with the chancellor, and have the princess lose her temper and slight the chancellor in front of him.

paras.zh: 吴起看见公主轻贱魏相，果然辞掉了这门婚事。武侯因此疑心他，不再相信他。吴起怕获罪，就离开魏国，去了楚国。
paras.en: Wu Qi saw the princess slighting the chancellor of Wei, and sure enough he declined the match. Marquis Wu drew suspicion from this and no longer believed him. Wu Qi, afraid of the consequences, left Wei and went on to Chu.

paras.zh: 到楚国后，楚悼王素闻其贤，用他为相。他明定法令、审慎号令，裁去不急需的官员，罢废与王室疏远的公族，重点在强兵，破除纵横游说之辞；于是南平百越，北并陈蔡，击退三晋，西伐秦国，诸侯以此为患。楚国的贵戚都想害他。悼王死后，宗室大臣作乱攻打吴起，吴起跑到悼王尸体旁伏在上面，攻击他的人射刺吴起，也射中了悼王。悼王下葬、太子即位后，令尹尽数诛杀那些射吴起并射中王尸的人，因射吴起而被灭宗的有七十余家。
paras.en: King Dao of Chu had long known his reputation and made him chancellor on arrival. Wu Qi laid down clear laws and careful orders, cut away the offices that were not needed, removed distant members of the royal clan, bent everything toward a strong army, and swept away the talk of the persuaders who argued for the vertical and horizontal alliances. Chu then pacified the Hundred Yue in the south, absorbed Chen and Cai in the north, repelled the Three Jin, and struck west against Qin. The other lords began to fear Chu's strength. Every nobleman of royal blood wanted him dead. When King Dao died, men of the royal house and the great ministers rose in revolt and attacked Wu Qi; he ran to the dead king's body and flung himself over it. Those hunting him shot and stabbed at Wu Qi — and hit the corpse of the king as well. Once the king was buried and the crown prince on the throne, the chief minister was ordered to execute everyone who had shot at Wu Qi and struck the royal body; more than seventy clans were destroyed for their part in it.

paras.zh: 回头看这套设计，它把一个说不清的问题（他心里留不留），换成了一个看得见的动作（接不接婚事）。仆人对吴起的判断是：「吳起為人節廉而自喜名也。」这是史书的记述，不是本文替他写的人格。一种解释是，计策能成，靠的是吴起见公主贱魏相就不肯接受这门亲事：看见主家受辱还答应婚事，与仆人所描述的那种自惜名声的性情不合。他的举动正如仆人所料，落进了别人按这一判断画好的框里。（作者解释）
paras.en: Step back and look at the design. It trades an unanswerable question — does he mean to stay? — for a visible act: does he accept the marriage? The servant's reading of Wu Qi is on the record — in translation, that he was a man of integrity and restraint who cherished his good name. That is the history's description of him, not a sketch invented here. One explanation for the scheme's success: Wu Qi, seeing the princess treat the chancellor so cheaply, declined the match. Agreeing to a marriage while the household he was visiting was being humiliated would not fit the name-cherishing character the servant attributed to him. He acted just as the servant had predicted, and stepped into a frame drawn around that reading of his character.

paras.zh: 关键的一句是「武侯疑之而弗信也」。原文没有写吴起做任何辩解，只写他「懼得罪，遂去」。作者推断，他可能判断解释已经无用，也可能担心解释本身会被当成“无留心”的又一件证据。作者提出的替代选择是：当场把这场会面的经过讲给武侯，或者暂缓决定、等待下一次自证的机会；但原文没有写他考虑过这些选项。（作者推断）
paras.en: The key sentence is the one in which, in translation, Marquis Wu grew suspicious and no longer believed him. The source records no defense by Wu Qi; it says only that he feared being punished and so left. The author infers that he may have judged explanation already useless, or that he worried the explanation itself would be taken as one more piece of evidence that he had no intention of staying. The alternative the author would put on the table: tell Marquis Wu on the spot what had happened at that meeting, or hold off on any decision and wait for another chance to prove himself. The source says nothing about his weighing such options.

paras.zh: 司马迁在篇末的评语是：「吳起說武侯以形勢不如德，然行之於楚，以刻暴少恩亡其軀。」这句话把西河边那番「在德不在險」与他在楚的结局并置。它是史家的评断，本文只把它当作一段记述呈现；它不是吴起离开魏国那天能预见的答案。
paras.en: Sima Qian closes the biography with this verdict, rendered here in translation: Wu Qi urged Marquis Wu that strength of position was no substitute for virtue, yet when he acted in Chu, cruelty and a want of kindness cost him his life — how sad. The line sets the words he spoke beside the West River against his end in Chu. It is the historian's judgment, and this article presents it only as a record — not as an answer Wu Qi could have seen coming on the day he left Wei.

heading.en: A Small Test Arranged for You

paras.zh: 现代团队里，功劳清楚的人也会遇到类似的小事：一次被安排的表态、一场本不必他参加的会、一个“随口”问出的问题。考的不是业绩，是立场。有人当场发作，把不满说得很满，第二天人人都知道“他果然待不久”；试探本身说明不了什么，反应先说明了一切。
paras.en: In modern teams, people with clear credit run into small arrangements of the same kind: a staged declaration of loyalty, a meeting they had no need to attend, a question thrown out casually. What is being tested is not performance but position. Some blow up on the spot and pour out their grievance, and by the next day everyone knows he will not be around long. The test itself proves nothing; the reaction proves everything.

paras.zh: 也有人察觉这是试探，既不接招也不吵，回去把手上那件能自证的事做完，等结果落地再谈去留。差别常常不在功劳簿的厚度，而在怀疑走到哪一步：还在“有疑”的阶段，事实可以说话；到了“不再信”的阶段，同一件事只会被重新解释一遍。
paras.en: Others see through the test. They neither take the bait nor quarrel; they go back and finish the one piece of work in hand that can speak for them, and discuss leaving or staying once the results are in. The difference is often not the thickness of the record of achievement but the stage suspicion has reached: while it is still only doubt, facts can talk; once trust is gone, the same facts will only be reinterpreted.

paras.zh: 本篇只有一个史源：《史記·孫子吳起列傳》。吴起与田文的对话、士卒母亲的哭诉、公叔之仆的计策，都是史书中的叙述，未必是逐字实录；本文不替吴起补写心理活动。原文没有公元纪年，本文也不作换算。
paras.en: This piece rests on a single source: the "Account of Sunzi and Wu Qi" in Sima Qian's Records of the Grand Historian. The exchange between Wu Qi and Tian Wen, the weeping of the soldier's mother, and the servant's scheme are all narratives within that history and need not be verbatim transcripts. The article does not invent Wu Qi's inner life. The original gives no dates in the common era, and none have been calculated here.

paras.zh: 吴起在楚的改革与身死，原文叙述简略：能确认的是明法审令、裁去不急之官、废公族疏远者，以及南平百越、北并陈蔡、却三晋、西伐秦这些记述，此外的细节本文不再补写。上文与下文中标注为作者推断、作者提出的替代选择，均属解释与反事实，用于讨论，不构成史实。
paras.en: The account of Wu Qi's reforms in Chu and of his death is brief. What can be confirmed is the clearing of laws and orders, the cutting of unneeded offices, the removal of distant members of the royal clan, and the campaigns — south against the Hundred Yue, north absorbing Chen and Cai, repelling the Three Jin, west against Qin. Beyond these the article adds nothing. Wherever the text above or below marks a view as an authorial inference or an author's alternative, it is interpretation and counterfactual, offered for discussion, not history.

scenario.zh: 一家小公司里，一位功劳清楚的核心成员被安排了一次试探：管理层假装公司要与另一家合并，想看他是立刻站队还是观望。他看出这是试探后当场请辞，管理层反而觉得坐实了他“无留心”。
scenario.en: In a small company, a core member with an unmistakable record is handed a staged test: management pretends the firm is about to merge with another, to see whether he immediately picks a side or watches and waits. He sees through the arrangement and resigns on the spot — and management reads the resignation as proof that he never meant to stay.

question.zh: 当你发现信任正被设计成一次考核，什么时候该解释、什么时候该等一等、什么时候该走？判断的依据应该是怀疑的程度，还是自己手上有没有能自证的事？
question.en: When you see trust being engineered into an examination, when should you explain, when should you wait, and when should you walk? Should the call rest on how far suspicion has already travelled, or on whether you hold something in hand that can speak for you?

assumptions.zh:
怀疑已经公开，不再只是传闻
试探已经执行，且不止一次的可能
还存在一条可以直接对话的渠道
手上有一件近期能出结果、能自证的事
assumptions.en:
Suspicion is already open, not mere rumor.
The test has been run, and may well be run again.
A direct channel of conversation is still open.
One piece of work in your hands will land soon and can speak for you.

steps.zh:
先分辨这是考核还是结论：若是考核，反应本身就是答卷；若是结论，解释只是补材料。
找一件两三周内能落地的事，用结果说话，而不是用表态说话。
同时看怀疑的走向：若试探接连出现、且不给解释机会，说明问题不在信息，在立场。
steps.en:
First decide whether this is a test or a verdict: if it is a test, your reaction is the answer sheet; if it is a verdict, explanation is only extra paperwork.
Find something that can land within two or three weeks, and let the result speak rather than declarations.
Watch which way suspicion is moving: if tests come one after another and no chance to explain is given, the problem is not information but position.

alternative.zh: 作者提出的替代选择：既不按剧本接招，也不当场离开，而是把这场安排摊开说破，逼对方把“留不留心”的判断变成一次明面的对话。代价是可能被视为挑衅，收益是把暗处的试探变成明处的谈判。
alternative.en: The author's alternative: neither play the part you have been handed nor walk out on the spot, but call the arrangement by its name and force the question of whether he means to stay into an open negotiation. The cost is being read as provocative; the gain is turning a test staged in the dark into a bargain made in the light.

uncertainty_note.zh: 本篇史源单一，仅《史記·孫子吳起列傳》；文中对话、卒母之哭、公叔之仆的计策皆为史书记述，未必逐字实录；原文无公元纪年，本文不作换算；吴起在楚的改革与身死叙述简略，未补写细节；文中“一种解释是”“作者推断”及作者提出的替代选择均属作者解释，不是史料记载。
uncertainty_note.en: This piece draws on a single source, the "Account of Sunzi and Wu Qi" in the Records of the Grand Historian. The dialogues, the soldier's mother's tears, and the servant's scheme are the history's narratives and need not be verbatim; the original carries no common-era dates and none have been converted; Wu Qi's reforms and death in Chu are told briefly and no detail has been added; every "one explanation" and "the author infers", and the author's alternative, are interpretation, not recorded history.

preheader.en: When the doubt starts with a staged test instead of the work itself: why Wu Qi chose to leave
